chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man: is it permissible for him to look at his wife when she dies and to perform ghusl (ritual washing) for her if there is no one with him to wash her? And about the woman: may she look at the like of that from her husband when he dies? He said: “There is no harm in that. Rather, the family of the woman only does that out of dislike that her husband should look at something they dislike.”

key_terms.أَيَصْلُحُ: whether it is proper or legally permissible
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.يَنْظُرَ: to look at the deceased spouse's body
key_terms.يُغَسِّلَهَا: to perform ghusl (ritual washing) for her after death

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife look at and wash their spouse after death in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning spouses at the time of death, stating that there is no objection to a husband looking at and washing his deceased wife, and likewise regarding the wife and her deceased husband. It also explains that when the woman's family undertakes this instead, it is due to their own dislike, not because the act is unlawful.
